title: Dynamic MCS Ordering Maintenance
summary: A fully-dynamic Maximum-Cardinality-Search (MCS) ordering algorithm that, on a single-edge insertion or deletion into a loop-free undirected graph, scans the affected window between the two endpoints for the first step at which the current ordering's choice stops being a legal MCS pick, and only then regreedies the suffix (probe-then-repair). Correctness - every order produced stays a valid MCS ordering of the updated graph, and in fact equals the from-scratch canonical ordering - is machine-checked in Lean 4 / Mathlib, together with locality (the first position whose choice can change lies…

review.reason: Fully dynamic maximum-cardinality-search ordering maintenance with machine-checked correctness and locality.
